skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automate browser sessions through inference.sh. Open pages, interact with elements, fill forms, capture screenshots or video, and run controlled page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Run browser workflows, screenshots, forms, and page checks through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-sh-0

security_audit.summary: The skill provides useful browser automation, but it relies on shell-driven infsh workflows, remote browser capture, proxy support, file upload, and page JavaScript execution. The critical issue is the pipe-to-shell installer; additional high-risk content includes cookie extraction guidance and proxy rotation for rate-limit avoidance. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell quick start with a signed release download, checksum verification, and separate install command.

remediation.issue: Authenticated session guidance includes cookie extraction and sensitive capture workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples and require explicit consent before screenshots, videos, file uploads, or JavaScript on authenticated pages.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation includes rate-limit avoidance and anonymity use cases.
remediation.suggestion: Limit proxy examples to legitimate geo-testing and corporate access, and remove evasion-oriented scraping examples.

remediation.issue: Shell templates interpolate user input into command-line JSON payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Build JSON payloads with a structured encoder, validate target URLs, and quote session identifiers consistently.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript execution and local file upload are broad browser capabilities.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear approval gates and warnings before executing page JavaScript or uploading local files to external websites.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Web tasks often require repeated navigation, form entry, and visual checks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured browser workflow through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Open URLs in a managed browser session and keep session state across actions.
Return compact @e element references for clicks, typing, selection, scrolling, and navigation.
Capture viewport or full-page screenshots and optional session videos.
Run JavaScript in the current page to inspect text, links, elements, and page state.
Support proxy settings, authenticated sessions, file uploads, and reusable shell workflow templates.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated infsh account before use.
Browser traffic, screenshots, videos, and uploaded files may pass through an external service.
Element refs can become stale after navigation, dynamic updates, or form submissions.
Templates need user review before use with credentials, private pages, or production systems.

use_cases.title: Check Web Workflows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser actions, capture screenshots, and verify visible results after each step.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Open public pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Automate Admin Tasks
use_cases.description: Navigate authenticated tools, fill forms, and record selected workflows after explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL with agent-browser, capture the visible page state, and summarize the main interactive elements: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to inspect this form, identify the needed @e refs, fill the approved values, submit it, and report the result: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence for a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this approved browser workflow, take screenshots after key steps, and explain any failed action without retrying destructive steps: [WORKFLOW]

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Authenticated Session
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm the target and credentials, use agent-browser to perform the approved authenticated checks, avoid recording secrets, and close the session when done.

output_examples.input: Inspect a pricing page and capture visible calls to action.
output: Opened the page and found the main plan selector, billing toggle, and contact sales button.
Captured a viewport screenshot and noted that the enterprise plan requires a separate contact flow.
No form was submitted and no authenticated content was accessed.

output_examples.input: Fill a test contact form with approved sample data.
output: Identified the name, email, message, and submit controls from the current snapshot.
Filled the approved test values and submitted the form.
The confirmation message appeared after submission, and the session was closed.

output_examples.input: Record a short workflow for a documentation review.
output: Started recording before the approved workflow and stopped it when the session closed.
Captured key screenshots during the navigation steps.
Flagged one step for manual review because the expected button was not visible.

best_practices: Confirm the target URL, data sensitivity, and allowed actions before opening a browser session.
Re-snapshot after navigation or dynamic page updates so each action uses current @e refs.
Disable video recording when handling credentials, private data, or regulated content.
anti_patterns: Do not run the remote installer through a pipe to shell without verification.
Do not use proxy rotation to bypass rate limits, access controls, or site policies.
Do not extract cookies, upload local files, or execute page JavaScript without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require another service?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated infsh account.

faq.question: Can it interact with logged-in pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but credentials and session data need explicit user approval and careful handling.

faq.question: What are @e refs?
faq.answer: They are compact element references returned by snapshots so agents can click, fill, and select page controls.

faq.question: Can it record video?
faq.answer: Yes. Recording is optional and should stay disabled for sensitive sessions.

faq.question: Does it support proxies?
faq.answer: Yes. Proxy support is documented for testing and corporate access, but misuse can violate site policies.

faq.question: Is it safe for arbitrary websites?
faq.answer: Use caution. Browser automation can trigger real actions, expose page data, or upload files if misused.
